name: developer
description: How software work fits together: tickets, branches, commits, pull requests, review, CI, migrations and releases.

memories.content: Ticket: a tracked unit of work (Jira, Linear, GitHub issue) with a key, a status and an owner
Branch: an isolated line of development, usually one per ticket
Commit: a recorded change with a message explaining why
Pull request: a proposed merge of a branch, reviewed before it lands
Code review: another person or agent checks a pull request for correctness, style and risk
Continuous integration: automated build, test and lint on every push
Tests: unit, integration and end-to-end checks that guard behavior
Database migration: a versioned schema change that must run in order in every environment
Staging environment: a copy of production for checking changes before release
Release: shipping merged changes to production
Incident: a production problem, its fix and what was learned
Typical flow: ticket → branch named after the ticket → commits → pull request → review and CI → merge → release
Schema migrations are hard to reverse: run them on staging first and keep them backward compatible with the running code
Small, focused pull requests are reviewed faster and break less
